title: Identify ringed tensor comparisons with specified adjunction mates
statement: Let $v:C\to D$ induce a geometric morphism $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ between sheaf topoi of sites small in the module universe, with $u_*$ given by precomposition with $v$ and $u^{-1}$ preserving finite limits [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $R,S$ be commutative ring sheaves on $C,D$, let $I$ be the specified algebraic inverse image of $R$-modules with coefficient ring $RI$ [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image], and let $\alpha:RI\to S$. Set $LM=S\otimes_{RI}IM$, on objects and maps, using sheafified scalar extension [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $P$ be direct image with scalar restriction along the adjunct $c:R\to u_*S$, with its canonical adjunction $L\dashv P$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. Assume its unit is geometric inverse-image insertion followed by scalar insertion $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. Suppose $P$ has the lax structure whose tensor maps are local pure-tensor pairings and whose unit is $c$. Then the oplax structure on $L$ obtained by this specified adjunction [lem-sfb-adjunction-oplax-mate] has tensor maps equal to the normalized canonical ringed tensor isomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison]. In particular they are invertible. After the inverse-image tensor identification their scalar-extension formula is $s\otimes(m\otimes n)\mapsto(s\otimes m)\otimes(1\otimes n)$, with inverse $(s\otimes m)\otimes(t\otimes n)\mapsto st\otimes(m\otimes n)$. The oplax unit is $S\otimes_{RI}RI\to S$, $s\otimes r\mapsto s\alpha(r)$, with inverse $s\mapsto s\otimes1$.

proof.text: Use the existing independent-universe inverse-image tensor comparison from CochainInverseComparison for the specified algebraic inverse image I. It supplies a natural isomorphism a from I(M tensor N) to I(M) tensor I(N), with its generalized pure-section formula. Its private pure-section restriction, tensor naturality and tensor generation lemmas apply definitionally to ringedComparisonPure.

proof.text: Use tensorObjIsoSheafification and siteTensorRightIso to identify the localization tensor with the explicit sectionwise tensor followed by sheafification. Naturality of the sheafification unit identifies their pure tensors. Transport scalarTensorBinaryIso through these isomorphisms. Its proved forward and inverse generator formulas give s tensor (m tensor n) mapped to (s tensor m) tensor (1 tensor n), with reverse formula multiplying s and t. Compose this scalar comparison with the inverse-image tensor isomorphism and the stipulated natural object identifications of L. Naturality of scalar insertion supplies q; the generalized pure equation follows from the two normalization formulas.

proof.text: For any normalized comparison, test its generalized equation on the product of the underlying sheaves of M and N, using the projections and their pure-tensor pairing. Evaluate at the geometric unit applied to (m,n). Naturality of that unit, the scalar insertion condition, and the prescribed module-adjunction unit yield P(mu) eta = p(eta tensor eta) on pure tensors. Tensor sheafification generation gives equality of morphisms. The adjunction hom equivalence sends the oplax mate to this same morphism, so injectivity identifies the mate with every normalized comparison. Its naturality follows from oplax naturality, and its invertibility and sectionwise formulas follow from the constructed isomorphism.

proof.text: Reuse the proved inverseImage_unit_iso from StrictPerfectRingedPullbackModel to identify I(R) with the regular RI-module by its underlying ring and module identifications. The graph equation for module scalar multiplication and preservation of one show that the inverse identification is linear. Compose this isomorphism with scalar extension and the scalar-extension unit isomorphism to obtain e0. The scalar-extension map formula and unit formula give e0(s tensor j^-1(r)) = s alpha(r). Its adjoint, evaluated using the stipulated insertion unit, equals the given ring morphism by the geometric adjunct hypothesis. Adjunction injectivity identifies e0 with the oplax unit. Applying the inverse of e0 to its formula at r=1 gives the asserted inverse. All arguments apply to zero rings and empty sites.
